title: Silicone Mat Turntable
new_elements: Unbreakable silicone tray mat (Replaces the glass plate and is dishwasher-safe.)
rationale: Nothing breaks and nothing needs careful handling.

title: Capacitor-Free Supply
new_elements: Direct-drive magnetron inverter (Avoids bulk HV storage, so nothing needs discharging.)
rationale: It removes a danger that users and repairers would otherwise need to be warned about.

title: One 'Go' button, each press adds a minute
new_elements: Single +1 min start button with tally lights (Press starts 1 minute at full power; each extra press adds one more; nothing else on the panel.)
rationale: A single control with one obvious rule is the minimum possible learning curve.

title: Doubler-Free Half-Wave Drive
new_elements: Direct half-wave magnetron supply (A higher-ratio transformer feeds the magnetron directly without a storage capacitor.)
rationale: It is cheaper and carries no stored lethal charge.

title: Toaster-Lever Start
new_elements: Push-down toaster-style start lever (Lever pressed down along a scale latches the circuit and pops up with a clunk when time is over.); Escapement-damped lever return (A spring and air-dashpot return the lever at a fixed speed, giving the cooking time.)
rationale: Every user already knows how a toaster works: push it down, wait for the pop.

title: Screwless Snap Panels
new_elements: Snap-fit assembly (Panels clip together with no screws or tools.)
rationale: Simple assembly keeps the product plain and uncluttered for the user.

title: Pictogram Food Dial
new_elements: 5-step power knob (Existing numbered power knob from base_product meta); Pictogram dial (Icons for cup, plate, soup, frozen and popcorn instead of numbers); Select by food picture (Maps directly to what the user is holding)
rationale: Pictures of food are understood instantly, unlike abstract power numbers.

title: No Stored Charge Design
new_elements: Zero stored high voltage (Energy is never held in a capacitor, so nothing stays charged)
rationale: Users never need to worry about a lethal charge after unplugging.

title: Daylight Light Pipe
new_elements: Shielded light pipe channelling room light into the cavity (Replaces the 20-25 W lamp.)
rationale: The interior is visible without a bulb that can burn out.

title: Gravity weight timer
new_elements: Descending-weight timer (Lift a visible weight on a track; it sinks over minutes and trips the switch at the bottom)
rationale: Time left is literally how high the weight is—visible from across the room.

title: Tap-Top Gesture
new_elements: Piezo tap sensor in lid (Each knock on the top adds 30 s, and a double-knock stops cooking.)
rationale: The whole box becomes one giant button.

title: Hold-to-heat paddle
new_elements: Dead-man's paddle switch (Magnetron runs only while the big paddle is held; release stops it.)
rationale: No numbers at all; user watches food and lets go.

title: Food icons on timer dial
new_elements: Timer bezel printed with foods at typical times (Mug at 1:30, plate at 3:00, etc.)
rationale: Guidance is on the knob itself; nothing to memorise.

title: Snap-Fit Modular Assembly
new_elements: Snap-fit tool-free assembly (Panels snap together with no screws or welds.)
rationale: Simpler assembly cuts cost, so the low-price tier can afford better, simpler controls.

title: Glass-Only Cavity
new_elements: Transparent mesh-laminated glass casing (Whole oven is see-through, no lamp or window holes)
rationale: What you see is what is happening; nothing hidden to understand.

title: Handle-Twist Controls
new_elements: Rotating door handle timer (Pull the handle to open the door, or twist it to set time. The handle is the only control on the oven.)
rationale: Every interaction happens at the single point the hand already touches.

title: Toaster lever microwave
new_elements: Push-down lever with depth stops (Press the lever to a notch (1–5 min); springs back up at end with a clack)
rationale: Borrows the toaster's zero-learning gesture everyone already owns.

title: External LED Light Pipe
new_elements: Outside-mounted LED with acrylic light pipe (Light is piped in through a sub-wavelength aperture, so it never needs replacing.)
rationale: It removes a maintenance task the user would otherwise have to learn.

title: +30 Seconds Mega Button
new_elements: Single large +30 s push button (Each press adds 30 s and starts the oven immediately; it is the only control.)
rationale: One button that needs no explanation: press more for hotter.

title: Silent Heat-Pipe Cooling
new_elements: Heat pipe to rear fin sink (Passive cooling of the RF source.)
rationale: Without fan noise, any sound the oven makes is clearly meaningful feedback.

title: Nonstick Ceramic Cavity
new_elements: Sol-gel ceramic nonstick coating (Splatter wipes off with water alone.)
rationale: Cleaning needs no special products or technique.

title: Lid-Keyed Containers
new_elements: Shape-coded container lids (Lid tabs press floor pins that select the right program.)
rationale: The container itself tells the oven what to do.

title: Tactile wheel with one notch
new_elements: Single-detent dial (One dial that only turns between Heat and Stop.)
rationale: There is only one thing to do with the dial, so nothing needs to be explained.

title: Glowing Cavity Walls
new_elements: Electroluminescent wall coating (Shadowless panel lighting built into the cavity enamel.); Even interior illumination (Replaces the 20-25 W incandescent bulb, which can burn out.)
rationale: Food is clearly visible, and there is no bulb to replace.

title: Plug-Free Induction Hob Link
new_elements: Hob-linked power bus (Cable that shares the power of the hob's induction coil.); Powers from the hob (The oven draws power through the hob's connection.)
rationale: A kitchen that is already wired for cooking needs no extra plug or socket.

title: Detent Dish-Size Knob
new_elements: Haptic three-stop knob (Clicks into cup, plate or bowl stops, each with a fixed time and power cam.)
rationale: A cheap mechanical knob gives feel-based choices with no numbers to interpret.

title: PTC thermistor replaces bimetal thermostat
new_elements: Self-resetting PTC thermal limiter (Resistance spikes with heat, throttling the magnetron without snapping contacts.)
rationale: Invisible protection that never leaves the user wondering why it stopped.

title: Door-handle twist is the timer
new_elements: Rotary door handle that winds the timer (Closing the door and twisting the handle sets minutes; untwisting stops.)
rationale: One gesture closes, locks and starts; there is nothing else to operate.

title: Door-close equals start
new_elements: Close-to-start door switch with fixed 60 s cycle (Shutting the door starts a 1-minute run; opening stops; repeat as needed.)
rationale: The only action is closing the door, which the user must do anyway.

title: Pictogram Dial
new_elements: Food pictogram ring (A ring of simple icons (egg, pizza, soup, leftovers) that sets everything at once.); Select food type (Choosing a picture selects the power and time automatically.)
rationale: Users pick what they are cooking instead of how to cook it.

title: Hardwired Wall Module
new_elements: Wall-box integrated microwave (Mounts into the wall like a light switch module, with no cord.)
rationale: It is always there and always ready, behaving like a household fixture rather than an appliance.

title: Neon charge indicator replaces bleeder resistor
new_elements: Neon HV-live lamp (Glows while capacitor holds charge, discharging it meanwhile.)
rationale: A visible 'still hot' cue needs no manual.

title: Living-hinge door
new_elements: Polymer living-hinge door with metal mesh insert (Moulded flexure replaces stamped steel hinges and pins.)
rationale: Light, soft door is easier for frail hands.

title: Pictogram Food Dial
new_elements: Single pictogram food dial (One knob with icons (cup, plate, frozen block, butter) whose cam sets both duration and duty-cycle at once); Dual-track profile cam (One cam shaft with two tracks: timer contact and power-cycling contact)
rationale: Users pick what they are heating, not minutes and watts, so there is nothing to learn.

title: Cup-shaped pressure pad as the only control
new_elements: Mug-silhouette floor pad that starts a drink program when pressed by a cup (Place the mug on the marked spot and shut the door; nothing else to touch.)
rationale: The student's 90% use case (reheat a drink) becomes a zero-input action.

title: Rounded Edge Cavity Mouth
new_elements: Soft-edged cavity mouth (A soft rubber lip around the opening makes the cavity safe to touch and reach.)
rationale: Soft edges make the cavity hard to hurt yourself on, so no caution is needed when loading.

title: Slider Lever Timeline
new_elements: Linear slider with food icons along track (Slide to 'coffee' or 'leftovers'; the slider returns as time elapses.)
rationale: Remaining time is shown as physical position.

title: Tray-as-Controller
new_elements: Smart food tray (Tray with an NFC tag that sets the program when placed.); Sets program by placing the tray (Putting the tray in starts the right cook.)
rationale: The tray carries the instructions, so the user never has to type them.

title: Recipe Card Slot
new_elements: Recipe card slot (A slot on the front accepts a card that carries power and time for one dish.)
rationale: Inserting a card works like playing a film, so the user just chooses a card and no settings.

title: Capacitor-free design eliminates bleed-down
new_elements: Resonant inverter without storage capacitor (No energy stored after switch-off; bleeder resistor and warnings removed.)
rationale: Removes a hidden hazard and its warning labels, making the product worry-free.

title: Tactile Braille-free big knob
new_elements: Oversized click knob (One palm-sized knob with 4 loud detents labelled by raised icons)
rationale: Few, physical, loud positions are learnable by feel in seconds.

title: Window Mesh Peel-Off
new_elements: Peel-off mesh film (A transparent film with a fine microwave-blocking mesh sticks to the door glass.)
rationale: A film is cheap, can be replaced in seconds, and keeps the door simple.

title: Sensing Stop, No Timer
new_elements: Humidity-based doneness sensor (A humidity sensor detects steam release and stops cooking when the food is hot, with no time to set.)
rationale: The machine decides when food is done, so the user never sets a time at all.

title: Magnet-Coded Containers
new_elements: Containers with embedded magnet codes (Reed switches under the floor read the container's code and set the program.); Reed-switch magnetic code reading (A cheap, passive identification method.)
rationale: The bowl tells the oven what to do, so the user just puts it in.

title: Phosphorescent cavity instead of lamp
new_elements: Glow-in-the-dark enamel liner (Strontium aluminate pigment in the cavity enamel charged by kitchen light)
rationale: No bulb to burn out or replace; the appliance never needs a maintenance step.

title: Tagged Containers Program the Oven
new_elements: Passive NFC tag reading (Reader in the floor reads a tag moulded into the bowl or mug that encodes its heating recipe.); NFC recipe reader (Replaces both knobs: the container sets time and power.)
rationale: The dish itself tells the oven what to do, so the user makes no decisions.

title: Egg-Timer Mechanical Cam
new_elements: Spring-wound egg-timer dial (A classic egg-timer spring dial with a bell that rings at the end.)
rationale: Users already know how to turn a timer dial and hear it ring.

title: Timer scale in food icons instead of minutes
new_elements: Icon-graduated clockwork dial (Dial marked with coffee cup, soup bowl, dinner plate at corresponding durations.)
rationale: Zero-cost substitution of numbers for meaning.

title: Door glass replaced by polymer with embedded mesh and printed tips
new_elements: Polycarbonate door with printed quick-guide (Cheaper than glass; instructions silk-screened directly on the window margin.)
rationale: Help is where the eyes already are; no manual.

title: Food Tokens
new_elements: Magnetic program pucks (Chunky shaped tokens (cup, soup bowl, snowflake) snap onto the fascia. The magnet pattern selects the program.); Hall-sensor token recognition (A magnet pattern on each token is read by a few Hall sensors.)
rationale: Choosing a program becomes as easy as picking up the picture of your food.

title: Thermochromic Window
new_elements: Heat-sensitive door window tint (The inner glass turns red as rising cavity steam heats it.)
rationale: A red window intuitively means the food is hot.

title: No Stored Charge by Design
new_elements: Capacitor-free resonant HV converter (Stores negligible energy, so no bleeder discharge is needed.)
rationale: Users and repairers do not need to know about hidden lethal hazards.

title: Pull-Cord Wind-Up
new_elements: Retractable pull cord (Replaces the timer knob; the length pulled sets time, retracting like a toy.); Proportional time gesture (A longer pull gives more time.); Spring-motor escapement (Reuses the clockwork mechanism.)
rationale: More pull means more heat, a mapping anyone understands immediately.

title: Picture-card control cartridge
new_elements: Picture-card cartridge (Slide-in cards each show one food and set all controls.)
rationale: Inserting a card for the food sets everything, so no setting ever needs remembering.

title: One-Button Heat
new_elements: Single HEAT button (One press starts 60 s of cooking; each extra press adds 30 s; no numbers or power settings.)
rationale: A single repeated press is the simplest possible interaction for a first-time user.

title: Temperature Target Dial
new_elements: Serving-temperature dial (A dial marked hot, warm and cold that sets a target food temperature instead of power.); Infrared food-temperature sensing (An IR sensor reads the food surface and adjusts heating until it reaches target.)
rationale: Choosing a serving temperature in plain words is far easier than choosing a power level.

title: Food-Type Slider Replacing Power
new_elements: Frozen-to-leftover slider (A slider running from frozen to leftover that sets power by food state.)
rationale: Choosing by food state is more natural than choosing an abstract power percentage.

title: Slider with food pictograms
new_elements: Numbered time knob (Minutes are abstract); Pictogram slider (Slider stops at icons: mug, plate, frozen box, popcorn; each is a fixed cam program); Select by picture (Language-free)
rationale: Users match food to picture instead of computing time.

title: Forever Light
new_elements: Externally mounted LED with light pipe (A 1 W LED outside the cavity shines in through a sub-wavelength aperture.)
rationale: The light never burns out, so users never face a dark oven or a maintenance task.

title: Fold-Away Oven Chassis
new_elements: Foldable shell (Shell folds flat for storage and unfolds for use, moulded from one polymer piece.)
rationale: A flat-packed oven that folds away suits a student's small room.

title: Thermal fuse instead of snap-disc thermostat
new_elements: PTC self-limiting heater element in magnetron mount (PTC ceramic raises resistance when hot, throttling current without a switch.)
rationale: Overheat protection becomes invisible and automatic; no reset button for the user.

title: Kitchen-timer twist egg
new_elements: Detachable egg timer (Standard twist egg timer docks on top and is the only control)
rationale: Uses an object people already own and understand.

title: Quiet Gravity Vent
new_elements: Rear chimney vent (Warm air rises through a single rear chimney, which needs no louvre design)
rationale: A single vent with no moving air is simpler to understand and safer to place near walls.

title: Fog-Proof Seal Without Choke
new_elements: Ceramic fiber gasket (Compressed ceramic fiber seals the door without needing a quarter-wave choke.)
rationale: A simpler seal removes the need for users to avoid bumping or misaligning the door.

title: Tagged Smart Containers
new_elements: RFID-tagged containers (Soup bowl, mug and rice box each carry a tag holding their heating program.); Cavity RFID reader (Shielded antenna that reads the tag when the door shuts.); Container-driven program (The vessel tells the oven what to do.)
rationale: Choosing the right bowl is the only decision the user makes.

title: Cavity Sound Sealer
new_elements: Silent operation housing (A sealed housing removes the fan and magnetron hum so cooking is silent.)
rationale: Silent operation removes the need to listen for a signal, so the user just checks the food.

title: Tilt the oven
new_elements: Rocking base timer (Tilt the whole unit back to wind a pendulum timer)
rationale: Playful whole-body gesture, no panel.

title: Mug-slot auto-run
new_elements: Mug-sized recess with microswitch that triggers a fixed 90 s cycle (Place a cup, door closes, it just runs; the plate area keeps a normal dial.)
rationale: The most common task—hot drink—needs no settings at all.

title: Inherently Low-Risk Architecture
new_elements: 48 V SELV internal bus (All user-reachable electronics run at safe extra-low voltage.)
rationale: Safety is built in, so users get no warning labels to decode.

title: Quantity Dial Instead of Time
new_elements: 'How much food' dial (Dial graduated in cups/plates; fixed power; time computed internally.)
rationale: Users estimate quantity far more easily than cooking seconds.

title: Water-Clock Drip Timer
new_elements: Drip-fed float timer (User pours a cup of water into a funnel; drip rate drains it, float drops and opens contacts.)
rationale: Mains-frequency independent and visually self-explaining: more water equals more time.

title: Modular Stackable Cabinet
new_elements: Stackable base unit (A flat base unit stacks under a shelf so the cavity is above the base.)
rationale: A stacking design fits small kitchens without needing counter space.

title: Silicone mat replaces glass turntable
new_elements: Flexible silicone cavity mat (Unbreakable, dishwasher-safe, drops in any orientation.)
rationale: No fragile plate to break or re-seat on a roller ring.

title: Auto-Start on Door Close
new_elements: Door-close start sensor (Closing the door starts the last-used cook program.); Starts cooking when the door closes (One action, no start button.)
rationale: Closing the door is already the last step of loading, so it is the natural moment to start.

title: Auto-Adjusting Voltage Core
new_elements: Universal input power converter (Accepts any mains voltage and frequency and converts it safely.)
rationale: The oven works anywhere in the world, so travelling users never face a voltage problem.

title: Fanless Heat-Pipe Cooling
new_elements: Heat-pipe to rear finned heatsink (Passive conduction cooling of the magnetron; no fan, no noise, no louvres to block.)
rationale: Silent operation removes the confusing 'why is it still running' fan noise after the cycle.

title: Food-Shaped Buttons
new_elements: Tactile food-silhouette keys (Raised cup, pizza-slice and snowflake buttons that can be found by touch.)
rationale: Shape tells the meaning, even to blind users.

title: Hinge contacts as the interlock
new_elements: Conductive hinge-pin interlock (Door hinge completes the magnetron circuit only when fully closed.)
rationale: Fewer parts to fail or confuse, keeping the appliance trouble-free.

title: Electroluminescent Cavity Wall
new_elements: Electroluminescent phosphor panel behind cavity window (Thin, cool, shock-proof glow panel replaces the hot incandescent bulb.)
rationale: A lifetime glow source means users never encounter a dark, confusing cavity.

title: Bleeder resistor replaced by self-discharging capacitor film
new_elements: Leaky-dielectric HV capacitor (Capacitor with engineered dielectric leakage self-discharges in seconds.)
rationale: Removes a part and a safety warning the user would otherwise need to read.

title: Self-Draining Transformer Winding
new_elements: Relay-shorted auxiliary winding (On power-off, a normally-closed relay dumps the capacitor charge through a winding.)
rationale: The appliance is inherently safe, so the user never has to know about hidden hazards.

title: Snap-fit recycled shell
new_elements: Snap-fit recycled polymer shell (Outer shell moulded in one piece from recycled polymer, with no stamped steel.)
rationale: A cheap moulded shell lowers cost and weight so the unit is easy to move.

title: Low-Voltage RF Stack
new_elements: Low-voltage capacitive RF drive (Drive with no stored high voltage, so nothing is left charged.)
rationale: Removing the stored charge removes the fear of an unplugged appliance still being dangerous.

title: Pull-String Toy Timer
new_elements: Pull-cord spring timer (Replaces the rotary clockwork knob: the further you pull the cord, the longer it heats, and the cord slowly retracts.); Visible remaining time (The length of cord still out shows the time left.)
rationale: A physical length maps intuitively to duration, so no numbers need to be read.

title: Single-Shell Stamped Body
new_elements: Deep-drawn one-piece cavity shell (Cavity and casing formed in one draw with snap-fit panels.)
rationale: Seamless interior is cheaper to make and easier to wipe clean.

title: Silicone Mat Instead of Glass Tray
new_elements: Dishwasher-safe silicone cavity mat (Soft mat on a fixed floor; nothing to break, slip, or reinstall wrongly.)
rationale: Eliminates the puzzle of reseating a glass tray on a roller ring after cleaning.

title: Recipe Punch Cards
new_elements: Notched pictogram card reader (Slide in a 'popcorn' card, and its notches set time and power mechanically.)
rationale: Users pick a picture card, a zero-literacy interface.

title: Traffic-Light Dial Zones
new_elements: Colour-zoned single dial (Green (warm drink), amber (plate), red (frozen) sectors instead of minutes and watts.)
rationale: Colour categories are grasped faster than numeric scales.

title: Close-the-Door-to-Start
new_elements: Door-closure start switch with default 60 s cycle (Closing the door starts a fixed one-minute heat. Closing it again adds another minute.); Starts cooking implicitly on door close (Shutting the door is the only action needed to start cooking.)
rationale: Replacing the timer knob with the door itself means the user only has to do what they already do: put the food in and shut the door.

title: Turntable is the timer dial
new_elements: Hand-rotated minute-marked turntable (User turns the tray to a minute mark; motor unwinds it back to zero as it heats)
rationale: The food's own plate is the control; nothing on the front panel.

title: Pull-Cord Timer
new_elements: Retractable pull cord (The user pulls a cord to the length they want, and it slowly retracts while cooking runs.)
rationale: A longer pull means more time, which is understood directly by physical length.

title: Container-Key Presets
new_elements: Magnet-coded containers and reed switch array (Mug, bowl and plate each carry magnets that select a preset.)
rationale: The dish is the program, so there are zero controls to operate.

title: Gentle Mug Sleeve
new_elements: Mesh-lined silicone sleeve for delicate items (A sleeve slows heating of milk or chocolate so it does not boil over.)
rationale: Power control becomes an accessory you slip on, so there are no levels to understand.

title: Solid-state RF with continuous auto-cook
new_elements: GaN/LDMOS solid-state 2.45 GHz amplifier (Low-voltage transistor source with continuously variable power and built-in load feedback.); Solid-state RF source module (Replaces magnetron, HV transformer, capacitor and diode.)
rationale: Closed-loop power lets a single Start button cook correctly without user settings.

title: Handle-Is-the-Timer
new_elements: Rotary door handle timer (Turning the handle locks the door and winds the time in one motion.)
rationale: Closing and setting merge into one intuitive gesture.

title: Silent Passive Cooling
new_elements: Passive vent grille (Vent that cools the machine by convection with no fan noise.); Silent operation (Runs without fan noise that might cause confusion.)
rationale: A quiet machine gives no confusing sounds to interpret.

title: Egg-Timer Shell
new_elements: Egg-shaped timer (A dial shaped like an egg timer that turns to a heat level and ends with a spring stop.); Familiar timer (Reuses the look of a classic kitchen timer.)
rationale: People already know how a timer dial works, so the learning curve is zero.

title: Thermoelectric Silent Cooler
new_elements: Thermoelectric cooler pad (A solid-state pad moves heat from electronics to a fin, with no moving parts.)
rationale: No moving parts means no fan to clean or hear, so the appliance feels reassuring.

title: Single Flat Glass Panel
new_elements: Flat touch-glass pictogram panel (A flat glass face shows three large pictograms for cook, reheat and defrost.)
rationale: Three pictograms replace a crowded panel, so the choice is obvious at a glance.

title: Picture-Menu Dial
new_elements: Food-icon selector (A rotary dial with pictures (popcorn, leftovers, frozen pizza) that set time and power together.)
rationale: Choosing a picture of the food removes the need to know what numbers or power levels mean.

title: Snap-Fit Shell
new_elements: Injection-moulded snap shell (A moulded polymer shell with snap-fit joints replaces stamped and welded steel panels.)
rationale: Snap joints mean the casing is cheap to make and easy to keep in shape.

title: Pulp-Molded Shell
new_elements: Recycled pulp moulding (Casings are moulded from recycled fibre instead of stamped sheet metal.)
rationale: A simple moulded shell is cheap to make and easy to recycle.

title: One Button Means Everything
new_elements: Universal single button (A single button that opens, starts, and stops depending on the context.)
rationale: One button with context-based meaning has nothing to memorize beyond pressing it.

title: Reflective Mirror Door
new_elements: Mirrored inner glass (Door glass with a metal-free mirror coating to show the inside through reflection.)
rationale: A mirror is a simpler way to check the food than any hole pattern.

title: Daylight Light-Pipe
new_elements: Acrylic light pipe from top surface into cavity (Pipes ambient kitchen light through a choke-protected opening; no lamp at all.)
rationale: Zero-electronics lighting that always works and never confuses the user.

title: Self-Lighting Glow Cavity
new_elements: Phosphorescent cavity coating charged by the window and room light (The interior glows with no lamp.)
rationale: There is no bulb to replace, ever.

title: Three Pictogram Buttons
new_elements: Food-picture buttons (Three large buttons showing soup, drink and frozen meal.)
rationale: Choosing by picture needs no understanding of power levels or timings.

title: Heat/Defrost toggle
new_elements: Two-position Heat/Defrost toggle (Defrost = 30% duty via one cam lobe; all other cases full power)
rationale: Removes four meaningless intermediate power levels.

title: Light-Pipe Window
new_elements: Room-light pipe in cavity roof (Shielded acrylic light guide brings kitchen light into the cavity.)
rationale: Removing a part that can fail means one less thing for the user to deal with.

title: Picture Card Slot
new_elements: Punched picture cards (Slide a laminated card showing a food photo into a slot; the punch pattern sets the program.); Card-based programming (A mechanical, low-cost replacement for the knobs.)
rationale: Users insert the card of what they're eating; nothing else is required.

title: Airflow-driven turntable (no motor)
new_elements: Cooling-fan-driven turntable turbine (Magnetron cooling air spins a small turbine under the plate; no separate motor.)
rationale: Fewer parts and cheaper, keeping the basic model basic.

title: Passive chimney cooling replaces fan and motor
new_elements: Natural-convection heat-pipe chimney (Heat pipes from the magnetron to a rear stack create silent draught; no fan.)
rationale: A silent appliance removes the 'is it still running?' ambiguity and one more thing to fail.

title: Pictogram Knob Faces
new_elements: Pictogram dial (Dial with icons for steam, snow, and sun instead of numbers.); Icon-driven choice (Shows the effect of each setting with a picture.)
rationale: Pictures explain what each setting does without any reading.

title: Metallised polymer shell replaces steel casing
new_elements: Injection-moulded polymer with vacuum-metallised interior (Lightweight one-piece body with integrated controls.)
rationale: Light enough for a student to move and position without help.

title: Snap-Fit Tool-Free Assembly
new_elements: Stamped snap-tab cavity assembly (Interlocking stamped tabs replace screws and welds.)
rationale: Lower cost funds the auto-sensing features that make operation effortless.

title: Fixed-Cycle Reheat
new_elements: Single-length reheat cycle (A fixed 90-second cycle with a stop button replaces the imprecise short-time timer.)
rationale: A fixed cycle removes the need to set any time for the most common use.

title: Single +30 s Button
new_elements: One momentary '+30 s' button (Each press adds 30 s and starts immediately; holding adds a defrost-pattern minute.)
rationale: The only control is 'more', which cannot be misunderstood.

title: Self-Rectifying Magnetron
new_elements: Magnetron self-rectification (The tube conducts only on one half-cycle, removing the HV diode.)
rationale: Fewer parts mean fewer failures for the user to cope with.

title: Passive Capacitor Discharge
new_elements: Low-voltage energy buffer (A low-voltage buffer replaces the lethal capacitor, so no charge remains after unplugging.)
rationale: No lethal charge means the user can clean or service the oven without fear.

title: Single-Button Reheat Dock
new_elements: Reheat dock tray (A tray that sits on the unit; placing a plate on it starts a reheat, and taking it off stops.)
rationale: Placing the plate is the only action, and lifting it off ends the cycle, so no button is needed.
